chapters.title: The subject assistant decision: prompts, retrieval or fine-tuning
findings: The routing fixture needed a stage-by-stage capability and evidence ledger.
The prose incorrectly called120 the admission threshold while the helper uses100.
A model-quality comparison needed conditional failure accounting and controlled alternatives.

chapters.title: Data-science task contracts and structured extraction
findings: Decoded-object validation, source parsing and numerical eligibility were conflated.
The count ratio needed an explicit unit and aggregation counterexample.
Unsupported fields and rejected records needed separate evaluation denominators.

chapters.title: Prompt and context engineering with measurable boundaries
findings: The whole-item allocator needed exact scope and a greedy-selection counterexample.
Prompt serialization was not separated enough from model behavior and authorization.
Prompt tuning needed a controlled evaluation and truncation ledger.

chapters.title: Corpus provenance, versions and evaluation isolation
findings: Integrity metadata needed separation from authenticity, access and applicability.
Current-only version selection lacked an explicit historical-time counterexample.
Corpus, chunk, index and answer identities needed a dependency trace.

chapters.title: Chunking, overlap, offsets and context budgets
findings: Chunk-count and duplication formulas needed derivation and exact boundary arithmetic.
Character offsets were not distinguished from bytes or model tokens.
Overlap needed an evidence-dependence and multi-passage sufficiency counterexample.

chapters.title: Lexical retrieval and BM25 from first principles
findings: BM25 needed a full numeric score trace and parameter-limit interpretation.
Document-frequency and chunk-policy changes needed a corpus-dependence example.
The tokenizer and default-only parameter contract needed honest boundaries.

chapters.title: Embedding retrieval, similarity and representation limits
findings: Cosine retrieval needed an exact geometric calculation and a coordinate-system counterexample.
The metadata exercise only compares dictionaries; it does not enforce an integrated retrieval gate.
Encoder quality, normalization range and approximate search needed separate evidence.

chapters.title: Hybrid retrieval, reciprocal-rank fusion and reranking
findings: Fusion needed exact score gaps and a constant-dependent tradeoff.
Duplicate handling within a list was not distinguished from correlated list evidence.
Reranker quality needed candidate and context ceilings with controlled budgets.

chapters.title: Metadata filtering and access-controlled retrieval
findings: The access fixture needed an explicit trusted-input and enforcement boundary.
Filtering after top-k required a concrete result and leakage counterexample.
Cache policy identity, revocation and equivalence classes needed precise scope.

chapters.title: Query rewriting and bounded multi-hop retrieval
findings: The graph walk's hop definition needed queue-state and complexity traces.
Fractional and Boolean hop budgets were accepted despite violating the intended integer boundary.
Query expansion and graph reachability were not distinguished from evidence entailment.

chapters.title: Grounded claims, citations and evidence-based abstention
findings: Citation integrity, claim support and world truth needed separate tests.
The extractive helper was described too broadly as validating a support map.
Abstention required a concrete coverage/utility tradeoff and computed-claim lineage.

chapters.title: Evaluating retrieval and answers with oracle controls
findings: Retrieval recall and first-hit rank needed cutoff and multi-evidence interpretations.
Saved labels were not distinguished sufficiently from observed model execution.
Oracle context and aggregate scores needed paired controls and clear denominators.

chapters.title: Paired reliability studies and family-aware uncertainty
findings: The family bootstrap needed its exact discrete distribution and estimand.
Paired identity, selective accuracy and severe-error gates needed different denominators.
The finite saved-label fixture required a clearer population and causal boundary.

chapters.title: Supervised fine-tuning data and answer-target masks
findings: Answer-only masking needed an indexed next-token table and explicit denominator.
Truncation preserving any target was not distinguished from preserving complete answers.
Masking loss terms was not separated from conditioning paths or packing boundaries.

chapters.title: Full supervised fine-tuning of a tiny causal decoder
findings: The tiny decoder needed an exact parameter/shape ledger and active-logit derivative.
The held-out prefix could be solved through a shared token shortcut rather than broad transfer.
The final training receipt used a pre-update loss while held-out loss used the post-update model.

chapters.title: Low-rank adaptation: dimensions, gradients and a real update
findings: Independent LoRA orientation, exact gradient/update and rank review completed in lora_depth.py.

chapters.title: Quantized frozen bases, adapter gradients and QLoRA limits
findings: The quantization example needed exact reconstructed outputs and an error bound.
Packed-byte accounting needed separation from Python objects and compute buffers.
Adapter improvement toward zero was not the same as recovering the original model.

chapters.title: Compare full and adapter fine-tuning on frozen tasks
findings: The full-versus-adapter comparison needed a complete trainable-state and hypothesis-space ledger.
Equal steps were not separated from equal compute or identical optimization policy.
Held-out teacher-forced loss and output-head placement needed narrower interpretation.

chapters.title: Preference optimization, DPO and the RLHF distinction
findings: The preference loss needed its derivative, curvature and exact first update.
A free scalar margin was not a complete normalized language-model policy.
Sequence scoring, reference state and factual support required separate contracts.

chapters.title: Fine-tuning embeddings and a small reranker
findings: The trainable retrieval fixture needed its first gradient and analytic decision boundary.
The pairwise reranker needed an independent update trace.
False-negative identity detection was not an integrated data-admission function.

chapters.title: Optional pretrained-model adaptation with pinned offline artifacts
findings: The optional recipe needed a current evidence ladder separating execution from quality.
Trainer-internal label shifting needed comparison with the earlier manual-shift fixture.
Pinned artifacts, same-environment repeatability and platform scope needed precise interpretation.

chapters.title: Structured tools for extraction, aggregation and data-science work
findings: The grouped-mean tool needed grain, weighting and causal-boundary calculations.
Finite inputs could overflow the naive sum and return an infinite mean.
A typed proposal and output lookup were not a complete explanation validator or live database tool.

chapters.title: Domain assistant boundaries: freshness, injection, budgets and traces
findings: Freshness needed exact inclusive boundaries and a distinction between publication and knowledge time.
The call counter needed attempt semantics and separation from elapsed-time limits.
A field allowlist was not sufficient to guarantee safe trace values.

chapters.title: Capstone: a grounded and evaluated data-science subject assistant
findings: The capstone needed an exact integration ledger identifying what was and was not connected.
Three correct statuses were not distinguished from answer coverage and semantic quality.
The optional trained model's execution/failure evidence needed separation from this extractive baseline.
